method: Each physical volume is one disk minus its metadata area, divided into fixed-size physical extents: extents per disk is floor((disk GiB x 1024 - metadata MiB) / extent MiB), and whatever is left after the last whole extent - the metadata area plus up to one extent of tail slack - is unusable. The volume group is that count multiplied by the number of disks, so its size is extents x extent size; an extent below the metadata area or a disk smaller than one extent is refused rather than reported as zero capacity. A logical volume is allocated a whole number of extents, so its allocation is ceil(requested MiB / extent) x extent, the rounding waste is the difference, the free space left is the group minus that allocation, and a request larger than the group is refused with the largest size it could take. Four 1000 GiB disks with a 1 MiB metadata area and 4 MiB extents give 255,999 extents each and 1,023,996 in the group (4,095,984 MiB, 3,999.984 GiB, 99.9996% of the raw 4000 GiB); a 3000 GiB logical volume takes 768,000 whole extents and leaves 255,996 free (999.984 GiB). Sizes are binary GiB and MiB as LVM reports them, values are rounded to three decimals, and text, negatives, exponent notation, fractional extent sizes or disk counts and out-of-range values are refused with the field named. Thin pools, snapshots, mirrors, stripes, PV labels and any metadata beyond the single field are not modelled, and the page calculates locally without touching a disk or sending anything anywhere.

sources.title: LVM physical volumes are divided into equal-sized extents, and volume groups and logical volumes are composed of those extents.
A logical volume occupies a whole number of extents, so its usable size is the requested size rounded up to the next extent boundary.
